FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 2
Pg. 31 He that Eateth My Flesh and drinketh My Blood Abideth in Me and I in him. (Jn. VI 57) As a reflection of the unity of God - a necessary feature of the Creator, all things created tend to become one. All things tend to unity. The Earth with the sun, moon & stars and the innumerable bodies of the material heavens, are goverened in this ten- dency to unity by a power that men call, "Laws of Gravity." Natural instinct bring the irrational animal kingdom together, while men and angels - all creatures of good will are drawn by love and by the law of charity to unity among themselves and to union with God. Hence the word universe, applied in fullest and proper sense to all creations; for "universe litterally means, "turned or tending to one, and we know that each individual in all creation and all creation together turns to one thing, - the glory of God. . Each individual in its way and all together as one, reflect the divine Unity of the ever adorable Trinity. "The heavens show forth, the glory of God and the firmament declareth the work of His hands," sings the Psalmest, and the three young men in the firey furnace at Babylon? "O all ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, praise and exalt Him Him above all forever! "But dear Christians, if all things tend to unity, or to union which is practically the same thing, if all things tend to unity or union why emphsise the axion. "Love Tends To Union"?
Pg. 32 He that Eateth my flesh and drinketh My Blood abideth in Me and I in him." (Jn. VI 57) . "Love tends to union" and, "in union there is strength." These are two common axioms: yet how beautiful they are! What a depth in their meaning! We all desire to be near those we love. Separation from friends for a loving heart means sacrifice in- deed.
